statement: The paternal grandfather (Ahn 4) was born in Canada, c. 1925-1942, to parents who emigrated from Czechoslovakia.
basis: Father born 1962. Maria Demko's birth record sits in an old-country archive, which makes her the immigrant generation.
test: Grandfather's birth or baptism record; 1931 Census of Canada; any obituary.
resolution: Štefan Duska was born at Senné, house 160, in 1929 (S-024, register vol. IV, p. 110, entry 43). He was not born in Canada.

log.note: Kevin states his father was born in Montréal in 1962 (S-000-5). Ahn 4 was therefore in Montréal by 1962. That fits a Canadian-born Stefan and an immigrant Stefan equally, so no move.
Refuted by record.

statement: The immigrant generation reached Canada between 1924 and 1930.
basis: US quotas of 1921 and 1924 pushed Slovak emigration toward Canada in exactly those years.
test: Passenger lists and Form 30A (1919-1924), Canadian arrivals 1925-1935, naturalization lists 1915-1951.

log.note: Štefan was born at Senné in late 1929, so mother and son were still in Slovakia then. Only the father could have reached Canada by 1930 (see H-029).

statement: Ahn 4 or Ahn 8 carried the given name Ján / John.
basis: The father's middle name is John, and the name is the most common one in the region.
test: Any record naming the grandfather or great-grandfather.
resolution: Refuted by statement, not by record (coordinator ruling X-001). Neither man is a Ján or John. Reopen only if a document shows a second given name.

log.note: Kevin names Ahn 4 Stefan and Ahn 8 Mihaly.

statement: The Duska male line is from Senné (Szenna, Ung county). Iňačovce enters through a wife's family.
basis: Two villages 4 km apart usually means a marriage between them. PR-6 places Duska households in Senné in 1930.
test: Baptism and marriage entries giving house numbers and the bride's village.

log.note: A whole desktop folder is filed under Senné. Weak support: it shows where the owner was looking, not what he found.
L-006: a village website places a Dúška family in Iňačovce in the 18th century. A lead, with no archive reference, so a modest move.
Places agent, 12 Nov: Senné lay in the Nagykapos district and Iňačovce in the Szobránc district, so district papers for the two villages are in different series.

Michal Duska is "of Senné" and Maria Demko "of Iňačovce" on the 1947 certificate. That is the pattern predicted. Held at the cap: one generation is documented, and a lead still places an older Dúška family in Iňačovce (L-006).

Places agent, relayed in ledger v8: Greek Catholics of Senné were registered at Iňačovce, so "Senné and Iňačovce" in family memory could be one household. The 1947 certificate still gives two villages, one for each spouse.

statement: The Duskas were Roman Catholic and the Demkos Greek Catholic.
basis: Senné has a Roman Catholic register (1831-1926). A Rusyn Demko line (PR-4) would normally be Greek Catholic.
test: Denomination column in any baptism, marriage or census entry.

log.note: The Senné material he kept is Roman Catholic (Diocese of Szatmár). Weak support for a Roman Catholic Duska line.
György Demkó is entered as Greek Catholic. Supports the Demko half, if this is the right Demko family. The Duska half is still untested.
Places agent: Senné was the Roman Catholic parish and Iňačovce the Greek Catholic one, with the caution that a village does not fix a family's rite.
L-006 and L-012: Iňačovce was the Greek Catholic parish seat and a third of Senné was Greek Catholic in 1904. The Roman Catholic half of this guess is weaker.
The Demko half is now documented across three generations: every Demko father at Viszoka from 1831 to 1883 is Greek Catholic. The Duska half is still untested.
Places agent, 12 Nov: Senné had 580 Roman Catholics and 238 Greek Catholics in 1851, and its Greek Catholics were registered at Iňačovce. A Senné family could be either rite.

The 1947 certificate marks Michal Duska Roman Catholic and Maria Demko Greek Catholic. Documented for Ahn 8 and Ahn 9. Not yet shown for earlier Duskas: the János Du[s]ko of 1877 has a Greek Catholic wife and a daughter in the Greek Catholic book.

statement: Maria Demko was born c. 1890-1910 in an Ung county parish, and her entry is in the Mukachevo Eparchy Greek Catholic series held at Uzhhorod.
basis: L-003: that series covers Ung parishes 1826-1938 and is the usual reason a Slovak-side record ends up in Uzhhorod.
test: Her age in any Canadian or Czechoslovak record, then a page-by-page search of the matching parish and years.

log.note: A Demko household in Ung county fits. But this family baptised a child in a Roman Catholic book, and a birth after 1895 would be a civil record (H-014), so the Greek Catholic series is less certain.
If the 1882 book is Greek Catholic (see H-015), a Demko daughter in the Greek Catholic series becomes more plausible again.

Entry 33 of this batch is a daughter of a Greek Catholic father and a Roman Catholic mother, entered in what the folder calls a Greek Catholic book. Between the two Catholic rites the daughters-follow-mother default was not always kept, so a Demko daughter could well be in a Greek Catholic book.

Her birth year (1906) is inside the window, and Solymos is an Ung parish. But the Iňačovce Greek Catholic register is reported to run only to 1898 at Prešov, and a civil record is now in hand, which favours H-014.

Places agent, relayed in ledger v8: the Iňačovce Greek Catholic church archive was damaged by lightning in July 1929 and by fire in April 1930, and the indexed register stops in 1898. A copy held elsewhere may be the only surviving church record for 1906. This does not choose between this entry and H-014.

question: X-Q-01

statement: The record cited as the 1869 census (PR-3) does not come from the standard FamilySearch Slovakia 1869 collection.
basis: L-004: surviving 1869 sheets in that collection are reported to exclude Ung county. The record may be from another archive, another year, or a Zemplén village.
test: The image itself: archive, fond, film or DGS number, and the village named on the sheet.

log.note: Places agent: the 1869 sheets for Ung county are held at the Berehove branch of the Zakarpattia archive, offline, not on FamilySearch. That fits a record found outside the standard collection.
Ruling X-009: without the record and its archive reference, a claim resting on context is capped at 70.
Places agent, 12 Nov: two more reports place the Ung county 1869 sheets in the Zakarpattia archive, one giving the Berehove branch, fond 7/2. Already at the cap.

statement: Jozef Duska of Senné no. 73 (1930) is not Ahn 8. The direct-line ancestor had left for Canada before the 1930 census.
basis: Follows from H-002. PR-6 gives the household but not its relationship to the direct line.
test: The 1930 census sheet for house 73 and the notes on absent household members.

log.note: Ahn 8 is stated to be Mihaly, so Jozef of house 73 is not Ahn 8. Whether Mihaly had left for Canada by 1930 is still untested.
Ahn 8 is Michal, so he is not the Jozef of house 73. But the family lived at Senné 160 in late 1929, so whether Michal had left by the 1930 census is open.

statement: The ten pages are a parish copy-book of circulars from the Bishop of Szatmár, June 1837 to January 1840, kept in the Nagykapos district of Ung county. They are not a register.
basis: Raised on first sight of the batch.
test: Signatures, dates, entry numbers and place names inside the text.
resolution: Every circular is signed 'Joannes, Episcopus Szathmariensis' or by his vicar general Josephus Linczy and dated at Szatmár; entries run in numbered order from 554/1837 to 8/1840; entry 530 cites a district meeting at N. Kapos on 14 May 1839; four entries deal with the district library at Ungvár.

statement: The copy-book belongs to the Roman Catholic parish of Senné itself and was filmed with the Senné register (L-001).
basis: Only the folder name says Senné. The text fits any parish of the Nagykapos district. The Kulin gift note of 1838 is the one local entry.
test: Film or DGS number and image numbers (R-001); the title board at the start of the film item.

log.note: Places agent: Senné was a Roman Catholic parish under Szatmár from 1804, and Stretavka (Kis-Szeretva) was its filial in 1734, so the Kulin note fits a Senné parishioner.
Ruling X-009: capped at 70 until the film or archive reference is in hand.

Places agent, 12 Nov: Štefan Rácz was parish priest of Senné from 1831 to 1841, so his name on the copy-book would tie it to Senné. Checked the two countersignatures on the pages in hand (D-001-01, D-001-06): both read "Revisum per V.A.D." with an abbreviated signature and no name. The test is not met on these ten pages. Held at the cap.

statement: No Duska is named on these ten pages. They were saved as curiosities met while paging through the film, not as evidence for the line.
basis: Folder is called 'Interesting Pages'. A full read found no Duska, Demko or Senné household.
test: Kevin's own description of why he kept them; a second read at higher magnification.

log.note: All ten openings read entry by entry. Handwriting leaves a small chance a surname was missed.

statement: Mihály Demkó (b. 1882) is the father of Maria Demko, Ahn 9. That would make him Ahn 18 and György Demkó and Mária Hreskó Ahn 36 and 37.
basis: The owner filed this under leads and named the file for Mihály, which is what a researcher does with a person on the line. A man born in 1882 fits as father of a woman whose son was born c. 1925-1942.
test: Maria Demko's birth or marriage record naming her father; any record giving her age.

log.note: Coordinator ruling X-004: the folder is called Leads, so the file name is weak grounds. Coordinator analysis X-A-001: if true, Maria was born after about 1902 and H-014 follows. Rival X-H-001 (she is from another Demko household) is on the coordinator board at 35%.
Both files in this folder are from 1894-1895. If that window reflects a birth year the owner had for Maria Demko (H-019), Mihály, born 1882, cannot be her father.
Ruling X-004 (ledger v2): the owner's labels and filing are priors and move nothing on their own. The B-004 cut that rested on H-019 is undone.

Still possible. This folder adds rival fathers for a Maria Demko born about 1885 to 1910 (H-023, H-024). A first Mihály, a twin of 1873, is marked with a cross, so the Mihály of 1882 was the couple's second son of that name.

Per the Demko agent's civil birth registration of 1906 (DM-D-008 @57861ad, cited, not read by this agent): Maria's father is Mihály Demkó, born at Magasrév (Viszoka), aged 24 in 1906. That matches the boy baptised at Viszoka in August 1882. Identity by name, place and age, so held at the cap (X-009). The Demko agent has it at 70.

Ruling X-017: necronym risk unresolved, because the Viszoka burials are not in hand. What is in hand argues for survival. This Mihály is already the second of the name (the twin of May 1873 has a cross). The 1906 civil record, as the Demko agent reads it, gives the father as aged 24 and born at Magasrév: a birth in 1881 or 1882, which fits the August 1882 baptism and not the 1873 twin, who would have been 33. No later Mihály to this couple is in the folder, which runs to January 1883. Stays at the cap.

question: X-Q-03

statement: Maria Demko is a sister of Mihály: a daughter of György Demkó and Mária Hreskó of Viszoka, born c. 1885-1900.
basis: Rival to H-012. The same couple could have had a daughter Maria in those years.
test: Search the same register for other children of this couple, 1875-1900.
resolution: Maria Demko's parents are Mihály Demkó and Mária Kocsis, per the Demko agent's civil birth registration of 1906 (DM-D-008 @57861ad, cited, not read by this agent). She is not a daughter of György Demkó and Mária Hreskó.

log.note: Same reasoning: a birth around 1894-1895 fits a daughter of György Demkó and Mária Hreskó.
Same ruling. The B-004 rise that rested on H-019 is undone.
Mária Hreskó was already a mother in January 1857 (D-004-13). She cannot plausibly have borne a daughter late enough to be the grandmother of a man born in 1962.
Refuted.

question: X-Q-03

statement: Maria Demko was born after 1 October 1895, and the record in Uzhhorod is the county copy of a civil birth registration, not a church book.
basis: Hungary began civil registration in October 1895 and second copies went to the county seat, which for Ung county was Ungvár. That explains an Uzhhorod location for a village now in Slovakia. Rival to H-006. This rule is recalled from training, not sourced (X-010); it can only suggest a test.
test: Maria's year of birth; the fond and series title of the Uzhhorod record.

log.note: First half confirmed: she was born in 1906 and a civil registration exists (the Demko agent's civil birth registration of 1906 (DM-D-008 @57861ad, cited, not read by this agent)). Whether the Uzhhorod record is the county copy of it is still untested.

question: X-Q-01

statement: The entry is from the Roman Catholic register of Čičarovce (Csicser), which served Viszoka.
basis: File name says Čičarovce. The mother and both godparents are Roman Catholic, and neighbouring entries note 'rom. k.'.
test: The page header or film title for this image (R-003).
resolution: The 1870s entries for this same couple, in the same column layout as the 1882 strip, name the officiant as 'Kubek József csicseri g.k. lelkész', Greek Catholic pastor of Csicser (D-004-08, D-004-09). The priest of 1882 appears again on 7 Jan 1883 as 'Csurgovich János ... lelkész' (D-004-20). The book is the Greek Catholic register of Čičarovce. Still missing: the page header and archive reference (R-003).

log.note: The Demko agent reads the officiant as Csurgovich, and on a second look so do I. That is a Greek Catholic clerical surname in this region. Under the 1868 law a son followed his father's church, and the father is Greek Catholic. The book is more likely Greek Catholic.
Ruling X-010: that Csurgovich is a Greek Catholic clerical surname is recalled from training, not sourced. No further movement on the name alone. Test: identify the priest and his parish in 1882.
L-007 and L-009: Viszoka's Greek Catholics belonged to the Čičarovce Greek Catholic parish, and Csurgovich is now sourced as a Greek Catholic clerical family.
Refuted on the entries themselves.

question: X-Q-02

statement: György Demko of Gönyű 24 (1895) is a different man from György Demkó of Viszoka 132 (1882), and the two households are different Demko families.
basis: Different wife (Katalin Jobbágy against Mária Hreskó), different county (Abaúj-Torna against Ung), about 80 km apart, both settled farmers. Demko and György are both common.
test: Marriage entry of György Demko and Katalin Jobbágy, giving his age, birthplace and whether he was a widower.

log.note: Coordinator, X-Q-04: one man with two marriages has not been ruled out. Held at 65 until the Demko agent tests it.

György Demkó of Viszoka had the same wife, Mária Hreskó, from 1857 to 1882. A move to Gönyű and a new wife by 1895 is unlikely. Held at the X-009 cap; the Demko agent should still rule out a second marriage.

question: X-Q-04

statement: Hriczko of Szina and Hreskó of Viszoka are two surnames, not spellings of one family.
basis: Different vowel and consonant pattern in clear hands, and different counties. The owner may have saved the Hriczko entry to test exactly this.
test: Any record of the Viszoka family spelling the name Hriczko, or the reverse.

log.note: L-010: linguists list Hreško and Hricko as separate surnames.
D-004-03: one clerk writes Hreskó and Hricko on adjacent lines for two different people.

statement: Neither child in this folder is on the direct line. The folder name records where the owner searched for Duskas; these two are what he kept from that search.
basis: A folder called Duska Baptisms that holds no Duska. Belža is far from Senné and Iňačovce.
test: The owner's reason for searching the Belža book (R-004); any record tying a Duska to Belža, Gönyű or Szina.

log.note: Rests on a folder name, which ruling X-004 treats as a prior. Kept on the board as a question about the archive, and it moves no other entry. Kevin has since said that everything given to this agent comes from his Duska folder (S-000-3).

statement: The owner was searching 1894-1895 because a later record gave Maria Demko an age that points to a birth around 1894-1896.
basis: Both files kept from this parish fall within thirteen months of each other, one a Demko and one a Mária.
test: Maria Demko's age in any passenger list, census, marriage or burial record.
resolution: She was born in 1906 (gravestone S-025; Demko agent's civil record). The owner was not searching 1894 to 1896 for her.

log.note: Rests on which files the owner kept, a prior under ruling X-004. It moves no other entry until a record gives Maria Demko's age.
This folder shows the owner collected Demko baptisms from 1831 to 1883, not a narrow window.
Refuted.

question: X-Q-03

statement: György Demkó, husband of Mária Hreskó, is the György baptised at Viszoka in September [1834], son of György Demko and Anna Samudovszki [?].
basis: A man married by 1856 fits a birth in the early 1830s. Two boys named György Demko were baptised at Viszoka then; this one has a brother János.
test: His marriage entry (about 1855 to 1856), which should give his age and father; burial entries for either György.

log.note: Ruling X-017. If the Demko fathers of 1831, 1834, 1838 and 1840 are one man (H-031), the Georgius of 1831 probably died and this György of 1834 is the survivor. Necronym risk unresolved: burials not in hand.

statement: György Demkó, husband of Mária Hreskó, is the Georgius baptised at Viszoka in [1831], son of Georg. Demko and Barbara Cs[encsarik?].
basis: Rival to H-020.

log.note: Ruling X-017. A second son of the same name three years later, in the wake of a cholera year, suggests the 1831 child died.

statement: The couple of 1857 (Georgij Demko and Mária Hreško, Viszoka 79) is the couple of 1873 to 1882 (György Demkó and Mária Hreskó, Viszoka 121 and 132).
basis: Same two names, same village, same rite for him. Against: a sixteen-year gap with no child in this folder, a different house number, and her rite entered as Greek Catholic in 1857.
test: Baptisms at Viszoka between 1857 and 1873; the marriage entry; the 1869 census sheet for Viszoka.

log.note: The Demko agent reads the mother's rite in the 1857 entry as Roman Catholic, and a second look here agrees. That removes one of the three objections. Held at the cap.

statement: Maria Demko (Ahn 9) is a daughter of János Demkó and Mária Szlekár of Viszoka, born about 1884 to 1895.
basis: This couple was still having children in 1883, and their daughters so far are Anna, Erzsébet and Zsuzsánna. Rests on the unproved premise that Ahn 9 belongs to the Viszoka Demkos at all.
test: Baptisms at Viszoka from 1883 to 1895; any record of Maria's age or father.
resolution: Her father is a Mihály and her mother a Kocsis, per the Demko agent's civil birth registration of 1906 (DM-D-008 @57861ad, cited, not read by this agent).

log.note: Refuted.

question: X-Q-03

statement: Maria Demko (Ahn 9) is a daughter of János Demkó, born 1875, son of György Demkó and Mária Hreskó.
basis: He is seven years older than his brother Mihály and could have a daughter from about 1898. Same unproved premise as H-023.
test: Civil birth registrations for Viszoka after 1895.
resolution: Her father is a Mihály, per the Demko agent's civil birth registration of 1906 (DM-D-008 @57861ad, cited, not read by this agent).

log.note: Refuted.

question: X-Q-03

statement: János Demkó, husband of Szlekár, is the János baptised at Viszoka in [1838], and so a brother of the György of 1834.
basis: Right name, village and generation. In 1879 he lives at Viszoka 120, next door to György Demkó at 121.
test: His marriage entry; the 1869 census sheets for Viszoka 120 and 121.

log.note: Ruling X-017: necronym risk unresolved. Burials for 1838 to 1853 not in hand.

statement: The father's surname in the 1877 entry for Szenna 72 (D-005-10) is a form of Duska, written Dusko, and not Dunko or Denko.
basis: Five letters, D-u-?-k-o. The third letter fits s or n in this hand. A surname Dúška is reported at Iňačovce in the 18th century (L-006). The owner's label reads Duska, which counts only as a prior.
test: Other entries by the same clerk with a clear s and a clear n before k; the same household in the Senné Roman Catholic register or the 1869 census.

log.note: Part 2 of the folder holds no Duska, Dusko or Dunko entry and nothing from Szenna 72.

statement: János Du[s]ko of Senné 72 (1877) is a direct ancestor of Michal Duska, Ahn 8: his father or his grandfather.
basis: Same village and, if H-026 holds, the same rare surname, one or two generations before Michal. Against: his wife is Greek Catholic and Michal is Roman Catholic, and nothing links house 72 to house 160.
test: Michal's baptism entry (his father's name); house numbers of Duska households in the Senné register.

log.note: Part 2 of the folder holds no Duska, Dusko or Dunko entry and nothing from Szenna 72.

statement: Štefan Duska left Czechoslovakia between August 1947 and September 1950, and the 1947 certificate was drawn for that journey.
basis: A sealed baptism certificate issued for a 17-year-old in August 1947, and his mother's death at Montréal in September 1950. The Demko agent holds the same view for Maria (DM-H-019).
test: Canadian passenger lists and immigration records, 1947 to 1950.

statement: Michal Duska went to Canada ahead of his wife and son, between 1930 and 1939, and they followed after the war.
basis: A common pattern (recalled from training, X-010), and it would explain a family reunited only in the late 1940s. Nothing in hand shows where he was between 1929 and 1950.
test: Canadian arrival and naturalization records for a Michal or Mike Duska; the 1930 census sheet for Senné 160.

statement: Michal Duska was born at Senné between 1895 and 1908 and baptised in its Roman Catholic church.
basis: He is Roman Catholic and "of Senné" in 1929, and his wife was born in 1906.
test: The Senné Roman Catholic baptism register, which is filmed for 1866 to 1912 (L-001).

statement: The Demko fathers at Viszoka in 1831, 1834, 1838 and 1840 are one György Demko with three wives in turn: Barbara Cs[encsarik?], then Anna Samudovszki [?], then Mária Vaszil [?].
basis: Ruling X-017, rule 7: a change of mother between baptisms to one father is a second marriage until shown to be a second man. The wives do not overlap in time, and 1831 to 1832 was a cholera wave. The Demko agent reads the same pattern. Against: György and Demko are both common at Viszoka.
test: Burials of Barbara and Anna; marriage entries of 1832 to 1834 and 1838 to 1840; house numbers.

statement: The Krak families of Jesztreb belong to the kin and godparent circle of the Jesztreb Demkos, and reach this archive through the Demko side, not through the Duska male line.
basis: A godmother read as Anna Krak[o] stands for a Demko twin at Jesztreb in 1877 (D-005-22). The surnames Mraz, Tamás and Mazur recur among parents and godparents of both the Krak and the Demko entries there. No Krak entry names a Duska.
test: A marriage entry joining Krak to Demko, Kocsis or Duska; the mother's maiden name on Michal Duska's baptism.
